content:
Interview-এ সবচেয়ে common question: "Severity আর Priority-এর পার্থক্য কী?" অনেকে বলে "Severity = technical, Priority = business" — মুখস্থ। কিন্তু interviewer বলে: "High Severity, Low Priority-এর example দিন" — তখন many stumble।

এই post-এ Severity ও Priority independently বুঝবেন, 4টি combination-এ real example, bug report-এ কীভাবে set করবেন, আর triage meeting-এ কী discuss হয় — সব practical Bangla guide।

---

এক লাইনে পার্থক্য

  • Severity = Bug software-কে কতটা ক্ষতি করছে (technical impact)
  • Priority = Bug কত দ্রুত fix করতে হবে (business urgency)

Hospital Analogy:

Severity = রোগীর অবস্থা কত serious (heart attack vs common cold)। Priority = কে আগে treat হবে — VIP patient-এর minor issue high priority হতে পারে, homeless person-এর serious issue wait করতে পারে (unfair but business reality)। Software-এ same logic।

---

Severity vs Priority — Comparison Table

বিষয় Severity Priority
অর্থTechnical impact — system কতটা affectedBusiness urgency — কত দ্রুত fix
কে set করেQA / Tester (technical assessment)Product Owner / PM / Dev Lead
BasisFunctionality broken? Data loss? Crash?Revenue impact? User count? Release date?
Change হয়?Rarely — bug nature fixedOften — business context change
Example fieldCritical / High / Medium / LowP1 / P2 / P3 / P4

Key point: Severity আর Priority সবসময় match করে না — আর সেটা normal। Mature team independently evaluate করে discuss করে align করে।

---

Severity Levels — বিস্তারিত + Examples

Critical (S1 / Blocker)

Impact: System completely unusable, no workaround, production down

Examples:

  • Application crash on launch — কেউ login করতে পারছে না
  • Database connection fail — সব data inaccessible
  • Payment gateway down — revenue stop
  • Security breach — user data exposed

Action: Immediate fix, all hands on deck, hotfix deploy

High (S2 / Major)

Impact: Major feature broken, significant user impact, workaround difficult

Examples:

  • Payment fails for all users — order create impossible
  • Search returns wrong results — core feature broken
  • Registration OTP never sent — new user blocked
  • Report export corrupt file — business decision wrong data

Medium (S3 / Moderate)

Impact: Feature partially broken, workaround exists, limited user impact

Examples:

  • Filter works but sort broken on same page
  • Email notification delay 10 min (should be instant)
  • Mobile layout broken — desktop works fine
  • Export PDF missing footer — data correct

Low (S4 / Minor / Cosmetic)

Impact: Cosmetic, typo, minor UI misalignment, no functional impact

Examples:

  • Button color slightly off-brand
  • Typo in help text — "Recieve" instead of "Receive"
  • Footer copyright year wrong
  • Icon 2px misaligned
---

Priority Levels — Business Urgency

P1 — Fix Immediately

Drop everything, current sprint interrupt, hotfix possible। Usually Critical/High severity match — but not always (see combinations)।

P2 — Fix This Sprint / Release

Current release blocker নয় কিন্তু must fix before next release। High/Medium severity common।

P3 — Fix When Possible

Backlog-এ queue, next sprint or later। Medium/Low severity typical।

P4 — Fix If Time Permits

Nice to have, cosmetic, low business value। Often deferred indefinitely।

---

4টি Combination — Real Examples (Interview-Ready)

1. High Severity + High Priority

Scenario: Production-এ login completely broken — valid credentials দিলেও "Invalid password" সব user-এ।

Severity: Critical — nobody can access system

Priority: P1 — fix within hours, hotfix tonight

Why both high: Technical disaster + business disaster — same urgency

2. High Severity + Low Priority

Scenario: Admin panel-এ user role assignment broken — admin wrong role assign করতে পারছে না।

Severity: High — admin feature completely broken

Priority: P3 — admin panel beta-তে, public release 3 months away, 5 internal users only

Why mismatch: Technically serious, but business impact low right now — fix before public admin launch

3. Low Severity + High Priority

Scenario: Homepage hero banner-এ wrong company logo — competitor logo showing by mistake

Severity: Low — technically small config/image swap, one line fix

Priority: P1 — CEO product launch event tomorrow, press will screenshot homepage

Why mismatch: Tiny technical fix, huge brand/reputation risk — business drives priority

4. Low Severity + Low Priority

Scenario: Settings page-এ "About" section copyright year "2025" instead of "2026"

Severity: Low — cosmetic text, no function impact

Priority: P4 — fix when someone has spare time, maybe never

Bonus: Medium Severity + High Priority

Scenario: Checkout page mobile-এ "Pay Now" button partially hidden — scroll without clear indication

Severity: Medium — desktop works, mobile workaround (scroll) exists but poor UX

Priority: P1 — Black Friday sale tomorrow, 70% traffic mobile

---

QA হিসেবে Severity কীভাবে Assign করবেন

Bug report করার সময় QA typically Severity set করে — technical facts দিয়ে:

Ask Yourself:

  • Core functionality broken?
  • Data loss or corruption possible?
  • Security vulnerability?
  • Workaround exists?
  • How many users affected? (all vs edge case)
  • Production or staging only?

Bug Report-এ লিখুন:

  • Steps to reproduce — clear, numbered
  • Expected vs Actual
  • Environment — prod/staging, browser, OS
  • Impact statement — "All users cannot complete payment"
  • Suggested Severity — with reasoning

Priority QA suggest করতে পারেন, কিন্তু final decision usually Product Owner / Dev Lead — business context তাদের কাছে বেশি।

---

Bug Triage Meeting — কী হয়?

Weekly or daily short meeting — open bugs review:

  1. QA presents new bugs — severity + impact explain
  2. PM sets/adjusts priority — release timeline, business value
  3. Dev estimates effort — complex fix may lower priority temporarily
  4. Assign owner — who fixes, by when
  5. Duplicate/invalid close

Healthy debate: QA "High severity!" PM "Low priority — feature not launched yet" — agreement or compromise documented in ticket।

---

Decision Matrix — Quick Reference

P1 Urgent P2 High P3 Medium P4 Low
S1 CriticalHotfix nowRareRareAlmost never
S2 HighCommonCommonIf deferred OKUnreleased feature
S3 MediumLaunch/eventCommonCommonBacklog
S4 LowBrand/CEOPolish sprintCommonCommon
---

Common Mistakes — এড়িয়ে চলুন

  • Severity = Priority same value — always copy P1=S1 without thinking
  • Every bug Critical — cry wolf, real critical ignored
  • QA sets Priority without discussion — business context missing
  • No severity in bug report — triage inefficient
  • Severity never updated — bug scope grows, still Medium
  • Ignoring PM priority override — QA severity valid, but respect priority decision
---

Interview Questions — Sample Answers

Q: Severity vs Priority difference?

A: Severity is technical impact on system — QA assesses. Priority is business urgency to fix — PM decides. They can differ — e.g. wrong logo is Low severity but High priority before launch event.

Q: High Severity, Low Priority example?

A: Bug in unreleased admin module — feature broken (High severity) but not in production, release months away (Low priority P3).

Q: Who decides Priority?

A: Product Owner or Project Manager — they know business timeline, revenue impact, stakeholder pressure. QA provides severity and impact data to inform decision.

Pro Tip:

Bug log করার সময় Impact sentence লিখুন: "100% users blocked from checkout" — severity justify easy। Triage meeting-এ PM-কে business context জিজ্ঞেস করুন priority set-এ — mature QA actively participates, passive ticket logger নয়।

---

পরিশেষে

Severity = technical truth (QA domain)। Priority = business decision (PM domain)।

4 combinations মুখস্থ করুন interview-এর জন্য:

  1. High + High — production login down
  2. High + Low — unreleased admin bug
  3. Low + High — wrong logo before launch
  4. Low + Low — footer typo

Mismatch normal — discuss, document, fix by agreed priority। এটাই professional defect management।
